text: dsh-rightbar-quicknav 是一款面向 DSH Web 客户端的右侧栏快捷导航插件。它把竖排图标轨道挂载到 shell.overlay 悬浮层，并从宿主右侧栏标签注册表读取可用标签。轨道收起时显示三个图标，悬停后展开，悬停图标可查看标题，点击即可打开对应标签。插件还提供键盘方向键导航与中英文界面文案，适合希望少点几次就切换文件、Git、任务等右侧栏标签的 DSH 用户。

dsh-rightbar-quicknav adds a vertical icon rail to the DSH Web client. It reads tabs from the host registry, shows three icons when collapsed, expands on hover, and opens a tab when clicked. Arrow keys navigate the rail, giving users direct access to right-sidebar tabs such as Files, Git, and Tasks.
想在 DSH 里一键切换右侧栏的不同标签页。
How can I reach a right-sidebar tab without opening the tab strip first?
dsh-rightbar-quicknav 的功能「右侧栏快捷切换」：在右侧栏展开按钮下方显示可展开的图标轨道，条目取自宿主标签注册表；点击图标会打开对应标签，键盘也可用方向键移动并选择。
dsh-rightbar-quicknav 的维护与更新元数据：活跃维护；距最后推送 6 天；提交数 11；更新频次 unknown；近 90 天提交 未知；开放 Issue 未知；仓库健康分 62/100（置信度 low）。

**Right-sidebar quick navigation for DeepSeek Harness (DSH) — a vertical icon rail that jumps straight to any right-sidebar tab.**

> English · [简体中文](README-zh.md) · [日本語](README-ja.md) · [Español](README-es.md) · [Português](README-pt.md) · [हिन्दी](README-hi.md)

dsh-rightbar-quicknav README · What it does：DSH puts every right-sidebar feature (Files, Git, Tasks, Terminal, Browser, Image Studio, Memory…) behind a tab strip you have to open first. This plugin adds a **standing icon rail** directly under the *open right sidebar* button:

dsh-rightbar-quicknav README · What it does：- **Collapsed, it shows only 3 icons** — almost invisible until you need it.
- **Hover it** and it expands downward to reveal every available tab.
- **Hover an icon** and its title appears in a compact bubble.
- **Click an icon** and the right sidebar opens straight on that tab — one click instead of three.

The list is not hard-coded: it is read from the host's own tab registry (`sidebarRightTabs.guide()`), so any plugin that registers a tab appears in the rail automatically.

dsh-rightbar-quicknav README · Through the plugin manager (recommended)：`Plugins → Add` and point it at this package (npm tarball or a local directory). The bundle patch wires the client half into the Web/Desktop profile.

dsh-rightbar-quicknav README · Manual：```bash
cd ~/.dsh/profiles/<your-profile>
pnpm add dsh-rightbar-quicknav
```

Then **restart DSH completely** — client modules are composed at boot, a page refresh is not enough.

dsh-rightbar-quicknav README · Requirements：- DSH `>= 0.2.1-rc.1` (needs the `sidebarRightTabs` / `sidebarRight` client services)
- React provided by the host — this plugin has **no runtime dependencies** and **no build step**

dsh-rightbar-quicknav README · Behaviour details：| | |
|---|---|
| Position | right edge of the viewport, `10px` gap; `50px` below the host's *open right sidebar* button |
| Collapsed | 3 icons |
| Expand | hover (200 ms collapse delay when the pointer leaves) |
| Tooltip | single line, auto-width, flips to the other side when there is no room |
| Jump | `sidebarRight.openTab(kind)` |
| Hidden when | the right sidebar is already open, or no session is on screen |

dsh-rightbar-quicknav README · Design boundaries：- Mounts **only** into the additive `shell.overlay` slot — never covers or replaces shipped UI.
- All visuals are **inline React styles**: the host exposes no `styles` service, so class-based CSS would silently do nothing.
- Geometry is **event-driven** (`MutationObserver` + `ResizeObserver`), with zero polling and zero forced layout in steady state.
- The anchor is the host's own button, located by the stable attribute `data-sidebar-right-expand`, with an `aria-label` fallback; if neither matches, the rail falls back to a default position and logs one warning instead of disappearing or mis-anchoring.
- Keyboard accessible: the rail is a `toolbar` with roving tabindex and arrow keys, `Esc` closes the tooltip, focus outline is keyboard-only.
- Respects `prefers-reduced-motion`; a render-time exception is caught by an ErrorBoundary instead of blanking the slot.
- UI strings are bilingual (zh / en) and registered under the `rightbarQuicknav` locale namespace when the host provides one.

dsh-rightbar-quicknav README · Audit：This plugin has been through a full audit and a follow-up remediation round; both are in the repository:

- [`AUDIT-2026-11-06.md`](AUDIT-2026-11-06.md) — full audit: scoring, findings, roadmap
- [`AUDIT-a11y.md`](AUDIT-a11y.md) — interaction & accessibility review
- [`AUDIT-perf.md`](AUDIT-perf.md) — performance & resource review
- [`AUDIT-2026-11-06-REMEDIATION.md`](AUDIT-2026-11-06-REMEDIATION.md) — per-item verification and remediation ledger

dsh-rightbar-quicknav README · Development：```bash
node --check client.js     # syntax
node --test tests/         # render smoke tests (zero dependencies)
```

The render smoke test loads the real `client.js`, drives the plugin's own `apply() → slots.inject → slots.register` path with a minimal React stub, and asserts that rendering and effects do not throw. It exists because a single undefined identifier in an effect once made the whole rail silently disappear.

dsh-rightbar-quicknav README · Releasing：Releases are published **by CI, never from a developer machine**.

1. bump `version` in `package.json` **and** the `VERSION` constant in `client.js` — they must match
2. add a `## [x.y.z]` section to [`CHANGELOG.md`](CHANGELOG.md)
3. commit to `main`
4. `git tag vX.Y.Z && git push origin vX.Y.Z`

Pushing the tag runs [`.github/workflows/publish.yml`](.github/workflows/publish.yml), which:

dsh-rightbar-quicknav README · Releasing：- asserts tag == `package.json` version == `client.js` `VERSION` (`scripts/verify-version.mjs`)
- runs the syntax check and tests
- publishes with **npm Trusted Publishing (OIDC)** plus a provenance statement — no `NPM_TOKEN`, no 2FA prompt
- **waits until npm actually serves the version**: `npm publish` reports success while the version is still in npm's processing queue, so a green job that stopped there would be a false positive
- packs the tarball and creates the GitHub Release from the matching CHANGELOG section

dsh-rightbar-quicknav README · Releasing：Local `npm publish` is intentionally unavailable for this package: its publishing access requires 2FA and disallows bypass-2FA tokens, so a local publish only lands in npm's queue.

If `github.com:443` is unreachable from your machine, `node scripts/push-via-api.mjs` pushes the same tree through the Git Data API (identical tree hash, different commit SHA).
